_partNote: The classes sit at wildly different scales, so each tile shows the single object that reads for its class rather than a shared form: an arch dam, a flywheel rotor on a long shaft, a field-erected insulated tank, a pressure sphere on legs, a container-sized battery enclosure, a hand-sized capacitor can, and a charging pedestal. Only the storage tank and the capacitor can are both cylinders, and they differ in aspect ratio, roof shape, and what sits on top.

partPrompts.1: A concrete arch dam seen three-quarter: one tall curved wall, bowing toward the viewer, thick at the base and tapering upward to a straight crest walkway along the top, with a flat sheet of impounded water reaching back from the upstream side. The curved wall is the entire subject. No powerhouse, no towers, no trees, no hills, no cutaway.
partPrompts.2: A flywheel rotor standing on a plain surface: one thick heavy solid disc mounted at the middle of a long slim vertical shaft, the shaft projecting well clear above and below the disc. The contrast between the massive disc and the slim shaft is the point. Not a spoked wheel, no blades, no gear teeth, no housing or vacuum vessel around it, nothing else in the frame.
partPrompts.3: A large field-erected storage tank standing upright, seen three-quarter: a tall smooth cylinder with a shallow conical roof, two or three horizontal seam lines around the plain outer skin, and a low ring foundation at the base. It should read as a big insulated tank. Not a sphere, no legs, no stairs or ladders, no piping, no cutaway.
partPrompts.4: A spherical pressure vessel seen three-quarter: one large smooth sphere carried clear of the ground on a ring of short straight legs, with a small flanged nozzle at the top of the sphere. The sphere standing on legs is the whole silhouette. Not a cylinder, not a tank with a conical roof, no pipe runs, no surrounding structure, no cutaway.
partPrompts.5: A containerized battery enclosure seen three-quarter: one long low rectangular container, clearly much longer than it is tall, with a row of tall double doors down one long side, two low flat cooling units on the roof, and a plain flat end. It should read as a shipping-container-sized box standing on the ground. No sphere, no cylinder, no cables, no cabinets or transformers beside it.
partPrompts.6: A single supercapacitor cell standing upright, seen three-quarter: a small squat cylindrical can only a little taller than it is wide, with a flat top face carrying two chunky threaded terminal studs set near opposite edges, and a shallow crimped seam just below the rim. It should read as a hand-sized component, not as a tank. No conical roof, no legs, no wires, no printing.
partPrompts.7: An electric vehicle charging pedestal standing on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: one slim upright post with a rounded head, a plain blank display face near the top, a connector holstered on one side, and a single cable hanging from the head in one simple loop. One object only: no car, no building, no parking bay, no signage, no text.
